Maintenance Report — MNT-0073-004

Asset: WELL-0073 (SW-24 Well 073, T350, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: flowline Work started: 12 May 2023 08:00 · Finished: 13 May 2023 13:00 · Well stopped for this job: 29 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Brian Coleman · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0073-0030 on 2023-05-11 Report written: 15 May 2023

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0073-0030 at 10:45 on 2023-05-11 found crude oil on the pad: about 4.4% of the pad area, estimated 1.7 bbl. The inspector noted: "Pooled fluid near flowline." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 3.3 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a threaded coupling on the flowline close to the wellhead.

Root cause

Corrosion under a failed protective wrap on the coupling.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 0% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the coupling.
  2. Cut out the failed coupling and the pipe ends.
  3. Welded in new pipe and a new fitting.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 369 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 295 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 1.5 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0073-004 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.34% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0073-005

Asset: WELL-0073 (SW-24 Well 073, T350, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: rod string Work started: 11 Jun 2023 08:00 · Finished: 28 Jun 2023 21:00 · Well stopped for this job: 421 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Megan Ward, Kevin Price · Contractor: Sandstone Rod & Pump Triggered by: inspection INS-0073-0034 on 2023-06-08 Report written: 28 Jun 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that the pump jack was running but the wellhead was cold and the rod load had dropped. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0073-0034 showed the wellhead at 40.4 °C with the air at 29.7 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A dynamometer card showed no load from the downhole pump, which points to a parted rod. Sandstone Rod & Pump's workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 16 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Root cause

Fatigue failure of a rod body, probably started by corrosion pitting.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 2 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rod string and located the break.
  3. Recovered the lower section with an overshot fishing tool.
  4. Replaced the damaged rods.
  5. Ran the rod string back in and spaced out the pump.

Summary of the fix: fished and replaced parted rod section.

Testing and return to service

Pump test showed normal fluid delivery and the rod load returned to normal. The well was returned to production.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0073-014

Asset: WELL-0073 (SW-24 Well 073, T350, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 01 Nov 2024 08:00 · Finished: 26 Nov 2024 01:00 · Well stopped for this job: 593 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Daniel Foster · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0073-0107 on 2024-10-31 Report written: 26 Nov 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that the pumper heard grinding from the walking beam and saw the horsehead wobbling. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0073-0107 showed the wellhead at 19.7 °C with the air at 15.4 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing. The well stayed shut in for about 23 days longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

Root cause

Bearing wear from long service and an overdue grease interval.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
  2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
  3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
  4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
  5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours: smooth stroke, no knocking, bearing temperature normal. The well was returned to production.

Asset: WELL-0073 (SW-24 Well 073, T350, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 20 Apr 2025 08:00 · Finished: 23 Apr 2025 03:00 · Well stopped for this job: 67 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Kevin Price, Brian Coleman · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0073-0130 on 2025-04-17 Report written: 24 Apr 2025

What happened

Field staff reported that the operator found an oil puddle under the gearbox. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0073-0130 showed the wellhead at 23.3 °C with the air at 21.3 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The input shaft seal was worn and the gearbox oil level was below the sight glass.

Root cause

A hardened output shaft seal after years of service.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Drained the gearbox oil into a closed container.
  2. Replaced the input and output shaft seals.
  3. Cleaned the base and absorbed the spilled oil.
  4. Refilled with the specified gear oil to the correct level.

Summary of the fix: replaced gearbox seals and topped up oil.

Ran the unit for 1 hour and checked both shafts for leaks: none found. The well was returned to production.
